comments.body: Can it check hosts behind a client certificate? Ours are on an internal network with mutual TLS and most scanners just give up.
Seconding that, plus a flag for a proxy. Half our internal hosts can only be reached through one.

body: Redesigning a registration form used by people who read slowly and mostly use phones. The county field has 47 options. A native dropdown opens a long list that is hard to scan. Radio buttons would take five screens of scrolling. A search field with suggestions needs typing, which many users find hard. Has anyone tried a two step choice, region first and then county? I haven't seen it done and I'm not sure it reduces effort rather than adds a step.

comments.body: Two steps is fine if the first level is something people know by heart. Do users know which region their county is in? If not, you have added a step that confuses.
Good point, and many will know their town and not the county. Think about asking for the nearest town or market and deriving the county from it.
In my market trader apps, a list sorted by what people picked most with the full list below worked better than any hierarchy. Common ones at the top saved the most taps.

body: Switched opt-level from z to s on a Cortex-M0 sensor firmware. Size optimisation made the sensor loop about 30 percent slower for only 1.8 KB of flash saved out of 64. Went with s and the loop fits its time budget again. The surprise was that a division in the loop became a library call at z, and the M0 has no hardware divide anyway.

comments.body: Did you try replacing the division with a shift or a lookup table? On a core with no divide that would help at any optimisation level.
Check lto and codegen-units too. Setting codegen-units to 1 with fat lto gave us 6 percent smaller code at opt-level s, without touching speed.
I know nothing about firmware but I know bundlers, and the idea that whole program optimisation saves space sounds the same. Does it cost build time as well?
How did you measure the 30 percent? Cycle counter on the device, or from a simulator? Simulators get memory timings wrong on small cores.
Pin the profile settings in the repo so they get reviewed. We had a release that went out with a different opt-level because someone changed an environment variable on the build machine.
1.8 KB out of 64 is under 3 percent. Was z ever the right choice? Unless a bootloader size limit forced it, I would always start at s or 3 and measure.
Sometimes it is a flash limit. With two firmware slots for updates the image has to fit in under half of the chip, and then 3 percent decides whether you can ship.

title: Gapless order numbers per branch when Postgres sequences leave holes
body: Accounting wants invoice numbers per branch with no gaps: 1, 2, 3 and so on, per branch per year. A normal Postgres sequence skips numbers when a transaction rolls back. Options: a counter row per branch locked with SELECT FOR UPDATE inside the order transaction (correct, but orders in one branch serialise); a sequence plus a nightly renumber of voided numbers (gaps hidden, but numbers change after being printed); or allocate numbers only at the moment an invoice is finalised, separate from the order. I like the third, but it needs a draft state everywhere. Which would you choose?

comments.body: Number only at finalisation, the third option, and never renumber printed invoices. If a number was given to a customer it is a record. Renumbering is also something an auditor will ask about.

Third works, but remember that gapless itself is rarely a legal need. Many tax rules ask for a unique sequential series and an explanation for voided numbers. Ask accounting whether gaps with a void record are acceptable. It could save you the whole design.
Printed ones don't change, yes, that is the main reason I dislike the second option. The draft state is the cost I'm worried about, it touches the mobile order screen and the stock reservations.

One thing to watch with a counter row: if a finalisation transaction is slow because it waits on something external, say a fiscal device, every other invoice waits behind it. Keep the locked section to the increment and the insert, nothing else.
Also decide what happens when two branches merge or one closes. Does its series stop, or can another branch continue it? Easier to settle before the first number is issued.
